items.title: Modernize dependencies and use built-ins
items.body:
I got annoyed with deprecated transitive dependencies in electron-builder and figured I would fix it myself.

I got a bit carried away, so this PR has a bunch of changes (though all good ones I hope):

- Replaced `fs-extra` dependency with built-in `fs` functions that are already available in Node.js 22
- Removed dependency on lodash (fixes #549)
- Upgraded eslint from v8 to v10
- Replaced `ava` dev. dependency with built-in `node:test`
- Replaced `ts-node` dev. dependency with `tsx`
- Upgraded `@electron/asar` from 3.x to 4.x (fixes #611)
- Upgraded `typedoc`
- Replaced `debug` with `obug` (this was to fix missing `debug` types but it doesn't hurt to reduce install size)
- Upgraded Typescript from 5.4 to 5.7
- Switched to ESM (shouldn't affect consumers since `require(esm)` is supported across all maintained versions of Node.js)
- Bumped Node.js engine from 22.12 to 22.13

Note that this PR subsumes #599, #598, #617.

items.title: feat!: migrate to ESM
items.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Sanders** · [Slack thread](https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/C0BD3CT26G6/p1790121070765109)_

**Before:** `electron-winstaller` is compiled to CommonJS (`"main": "lib/index.js"`, `target: es5`), uses `require()`/`__dirname` internally, and needs a dynamic `import()` plus `with { 'resolution-mode': 'import' }` type imports to talk to the ESM-only `@electron/windows-sign`. The `node:test` specs (#621) are loaded through `ts-node/register`, which only supports CommonJS.

**After:** The package is ESM-only (`"type": "module"`, `"exports": "./lib/index.js"`), tsc emits ESM, and `@electron/windows-sign` is imported statically. The `node:test` specs run as ESM TypeScript via `jiti` (`node --import jiti/register --test ...`).

**BREAKING CHANGE:** consumers must `import` the package. Since `engines.node` is already `>=22.12.0`, `require('electron-winstaller')` also keeps working through Node's `require(esm)` (no top-level await in the entry point), but that is not something we advertise as supported beyond the README note.

The branch now carries a merge of `main` (#621, ava → `node:test`) on top of the original ESM commit; the merge resolves the spec/package.json conflicts by combining #621's test API, timeout, and win32-only gating of the sign spec with this branch's ESM shape, and swaps the TypeScript loader to `jiti`. Since the repo squash-merges, the PR still lands as a single commit.

This follows the same approach as https://github.com/electron/notarize/pull/222 and https://github.com/electron/node-minidump/pull/100. Where they differ I followed node-minidump (the more recent one): `node:` prefixes on all builtins and `import.meta.dirname` in place of `__dirname`. Both references extend `@tsconfig/node22`; I inlined the equivalent options instead because the current `@tsconfig/node22` release sets `lib: es2024`, which the pinned `typescript@~5.4.5` (required by `typedoc@0.25.13`) rejects. The `.nvmrc` is added as both references did.

### Changes

- `package.json`: `"type": "module"`, `"exports": "./lib/index.js"` (replaces `main`), `types` kept; devDeps: `ts-node` → `jiti@2.7.0` (exact pin), add `@types/debug`, `@types/node` `^20.6.0` → `~22.10.7` (for `import.meta.dirname` typings). `yarn.lock` regenerated via yarn.
- `package.json` scripts: `test:unit` is `node --import jiti/register --test --test-timeout=60000 "spec/*-spec.ts"` and `tdd` is the `--watch` variant; `test` still runs `lint` first. jiti resolves the specs' `../src/index.js`-style imports to the `.ts` sources, so the tests exercise `src/`, not `lib/`.
- `tsconfig.json`: `target: es2022`, `lib: es2023`, `module: node16`, `rootDir: src`, `skipLibCheck`; drops the non-existent `typings` include.
- `src/`: `.js` extensions on relative imports, `node:` builtins, `import debug from 'debug'` instead of `require('debug')`, `import.meta.dirname`, explicit `import type`/`export type` for type-only re-exports. CJS deps (`fs-extra`, `lodash`, `@electron/asar`) are default-imported, since their named exports are not detectable by Node's CJS interop (`import * as fs from 'fs-extra'` would yield `fs.copy === undefined` at runtime). `sign.ts` now imports `createSeaSignTool` statically.
- `spec/`: same treatment (`.js` import extensions, `import.meta.dirname`, `import debug from 'debug'`); `spec/helpers/windowsSignHook.js` converted to `export default` (windows-sign loads the hook via `import()` and honours `module.default`).
- `script/select-7z-arch.js` (the `install` script) converted to `import`, since `"type": "module"` makes it ESM.
- `README.md`: usage switched to `import` plus an ESM-only note.
- CI workflows are unchanged (already on Node 22.12 / 24; jiti's `--import` needs Node ≥20.6).

### Verification (Linux, Node 22.22, yarn 1.22.22)

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` / `yarn build` (`tsc`): pass; `lib/index.js` is emitted as ESM
- `yarn lint` (`oxlint src spec`): pass
- `node -e "import('./lib/index.js').then(m => console.log(Object.keys(m)))"` → `assertSupportedArch, convertVersion, createWindowsInstaller, sanitizeAuthors`
- `node script/select-7z-arch.js`: pass
- `yarn test:unit`: 8 tests, 5 pass, 1 skipped (`sign-spec`, win32-only), 2 fail. The two `installer-spec` e2e tests fail locally only with `You must install both Mono and Wine on non-Windows` (neither is installed here), so those need CI (ubuntu with Wine/Mono, windows-latest) to confirm. No `ExperimentalWarning`/`MODULE_TYPELESS` warnings are emitted.
- `spec/helpers/windowsSignHook.js` loads as ESM with a default export.

### Open questions

- `@types/node` is `~22.10.7` to mirror notarize; happy to loosen to `^22`.

items.title: chore: upgrade to Node 6
items.body:
Resolves #291, #292.

I've added `pify` as an alternative to Bluebird.promisify as @malept  requested.  By updating ava, I was able to remove bluebird entirely.

I ran the tests in node 6.9, and they pass. I suspect the CI will still fail because it's using node 4.1. I don't know enough about the CI setup to change those values with any certainty.
